NextGen Fellowship, online exercise 3, task 1

Port and vessel identification

This picture shows the port area of one of Russia’s most important military shipyards. It is the largest shipbuilding enterprise in the country and it was founded during the Soviet Stalinist period. The port area includes relevant civilian facilities related to the production of oil and gas, including oil platforms to be deployed in the Russian Arctic.

Task

  1. Identify the port and understand its relevance within the broader Russian military ecosystem, in particular in the high north.
  2. Identify the most important Russian naval vessel in the port facility. You should be able to argue why you selected the specific naval vessel and why you found it to be the most relevant. Write a paragraph justifying your choice.

Tips

For identifying a ship, a good starting point is to use online software such as Google Earth, Cesium, ArcGIS Online Satellite Basemap, or any equivalent software. European Space Agency medium resolution satellite imagery can show if the ship has moved over time. For this exercise, we will use the latest imagery visualized by Google Earth (picture date to use: 30 July 2025).

You should start by measuring the length and width of the ship, then check what vessels have those measurements. You should also examine photos and plans of the vessel to check the color and designs (e.g. shape of the deckhouse, mast, radar placing etc.). Designs come in different shapes, e.g. traditional silhouettes. Other means of identification require reading ship descriptions and analyses.

While identifying specific vessels is possible (that is, what is the vessel in the picture), it is almost impossible for submarines unless specific reports are matched with the date of the picture. In Ghost ship – Russia’s secret naval fleet, published by NDC, you can see an example of a vessel being identified.

NextGen Fellowship, online exercise 3, task 2

Battle damage assessment

The picture shows a ship which was hit by a Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in the Black Sea. The question is simple: how would you assess the damage to the vessel?

Task

  1. Write a paragraph giving a battle damage assessment and describing why you came to this conclusion.

Tips

Start by identifying the type of ship shown in the photograph, then assess the damage by asking yourself what a good strike against that particular class of ship would look like and why.

This isn’t an easy task but your answers will form the basis of the discussion in the workshop that follows.
